A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FeDaL and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. The material supports comparison despite extensive rewriting and rearrangement.

before.justification: V1 reports original FeDaL experiments on federated representation learning, downstream tasks, ablations, and scaling behavior.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds severe-heterogeneity comparisons, detailed classification results, and uncertainty estimates.

M1.justification: The written method introduces learnable trend/seasonal scaling factors in v2 Equation 2 and changes post-perturbation alignment from feature matching to gradient matching in the main text. The DBE/GBE architecture remains. However, Appendix B still specifies feature matching, leaving the implemented alignment procedure unclear.

E1.justification: Both versions use UTSD, CTSD, LOTSA, and the same forecasting, imputation, classification, and anomaly-detection benchmarks. V2's detailed classification tables concern retained archives; its additional heterogeneity configurations vary partitioning within existing coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 6 newly includes a scored MOMENT imputation comparison, absent from v1's imputation result tables despite its general baseline listing. Table 26 also reports UEA comparisons with DTW, XGBoost, Rocket, and LSTM beyond the earlier UEA plot. Time-MoE was already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: V1 Section 4.2 inherits Section 4.1's pretraining defaults, whereas v2 Table 9 specifies LOTSA masking of 50% instead of 75%, patch length 64 instead of 32, and decomposition period 8 instead of 4. V2 adds H3–H5 partitioning settings. Its representation input length changes to 512 in Section 4.1 but remains 1024 in Table 9; these reported revisions do not establish rerunning.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix C.1 adds robustness tests at imbalance factors 0.7, 0.8, and 0.9, extending the earlier H1/H2 analysis. Existing component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity, bias visualizations, core-set t-SNE analysis, and scaling studies are retained or redisplayed.

E5.justification: V1 provides no repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. V2 Appendix C.8 first reports three-run averages, excluding zero-shot forecasting, and Tables 27–30 provide representative variability estimates across several tasks. Table 26 additionally states a classification standard-deviation bound. This establishes new reporting, not an increase in runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds severe-heterogeneity results, per-dataset UCR/UEA scores, MOMENT imputation scores, and communication costs, while removing v1 Table 2's separate 5% and 10% few-shot result blocks. Most retained scores persist, but some summaries change: MOMENT's zero-shot average MSE changes from 0.402 to 0.465. Such summary revisions are not demonstrated performance improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix B revises the displayed Fourier representation from A+iP to the amplitude-phase form A times exp(iP), and changes alignment-loss normalization. These are substantive mathematical corrections. No new theorem or proof is introduced; the IGC definition already appeared in v1.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain DBE/GBE-based federated TSFM training, cross-task generalization, and a federated scaling study. From-scratch training and efficiency against larger models already appear in v1, including its appendices; v2 foregrounds these ideas without introducing a distinct core contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of how additive bias reconstruction and regularization influence the backbone. Appendix B also qualifies the privacy interpretation: perturbation mitigates but does not eliminate leakage, and formal differential-privacy guarantees remain future work. V1's corresponding discussion lacks this qualification.

D1.justification: V2 Table 9 substantially expands implementation disclosure with architecture dimensions, hardware, EMA factors, scheduling, and core-set generation/server-tuning settings. Appendix B adds preprocessing and partitioning code, including H1/H2 definitions. The abstract and new reproducibility statement report a public code release absent from v1.

R1.justification: V2 introduces TSFM-versus-TSPM positioning and sharpens comparisons with personalized federated models and FFTS. It adds references such as Mantis and TimeMixer++, replaces the gradient-matching citation with Grad-Match, and removes the cited domain-bias predecessor by Zhang et al. The broader research context remains federated TSFM learning.

P1.justification: The introduction, preliminaries, method explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. V2 reorganizes material into a larger-model discussion, expanded appendix subsections, and reproducibility and writing-assistance statements, alongside title, author, and terminology changes.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 2, separates the former combined ablation/sensitivity figure into Table 2 and Figure 4, and summarizes representation results while retaining their full table in the appendix. It redisplays existing t-SNE and Time-MoE material, adds configuration/classification/uncertainty tables, and substantially reflows the document.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency and evidential support through detailed implementation information, classification breakdowns, stronger heterogeneity tests, and uncertainty reporting. Its explicit privacy limitation also improves claim calibration. These gains are limited by removal of the separate few-shot results and newly inconsistent main-text versus appendix alignment losses and input lengths. The evidence supports a modest overall improvement rather than a substantial resolution of the paper's weaknesses.
